info.name: Hopper API
info.description:
# Hopper API

VM Cloud Platform — Slice & share compute resources

Hopper slices a Kubernetes cluster into per-student VMs with credit-based
billing. This collection is generated from the gateway's OpenAPI spec, so it
matches the deployed API exactly.

## Getting started

1. Select the **Hopper — Production** environment (top-right).
2. Set `userEmail` and `userPassword` to your account.
3. Send **1. Auth & API keys → Login**. That is all the setup there is — the
   `session_token` cookie lands in Postman's cookie jar and every other request
   uses it automatically.

## The two ways to authenticate

**Session cookie** (what `Login` gives you) — httpOnly, expires in ~5 minutes,
refreshed via `Refresh session`. Best for clicking around.

**API key** — send `X-API-Key: hop_...` (or `Authorization: Bearer hop_...`).
Create one with **Create API key** while logged in; the test script stores it in
the `apiKey` variable and the collection then prefers it over the cookie.
Best for scripts and CI.

Collection-level auth is configured as the API-key header. When `apiKey` is
empty the gateway ignores the header and falls back to the cookie, so both
paths work without you changing any settings.

Two constraints worth knowing before you debug a confusing 4xx:
- A `read_only` key is rejected with **403** on anything that is not
  GET/HEAD/OPTIONS.
- Creating or revoking API keys deliberately requires a cookie session, so an
  API key cannot mint another API key. Log in first.

## Variables

`baseUrl` and credentials live in the environment. Resource ids
(`podId`, `userId`, `keyId`, ...) are collection variables that the test scripts
fill in as you go — create a VM and the rest of the pods folder targets it
without you copying anything.

## Rate limits

Per-user for cookie sessions and per-key for API keys, so a script cannot
exhaust your browser session's budget. Login is 10/min, and 3 failed sign-ins
per (IP, email) trips a temporary block. A 429 carries `X-RateLimit-*` headers.

## Regenerating

```
python scripts/api/generate_postman.py
```

Re-run it after changing any route or schema and commit the result.

exec: // Applies to every request in the collection.
console.warn('401 - run "Login" first, or set apiKey. Sessions expire after ~5 minutes.');
console.warn('403 - insufficient role, or a read_only API key on a write request.');

item.name: 1. Auth & API keys
item.description:
Start here. `Login` seeds Postman's cookie jar with the `session_token` cookie and everything else in this collection will then work.

For scripted access, run `Create API key` once while logged in, paste the returned `key` into the `apiKey` environment variable, and requests will authenticate with the `X-API-Key` header instead of the cookie. Note that a `read_only` key is rejected on anything other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS.

request.description:
Browser-only. Redirects to Keycloak for the SSO flow. Use `POST /auth/login` from Postman instead.

Begin OIDC auth with PKCE + state + nonce.

`GET /auth/login`

Direct email + password grant. Responds with the user object and sets the httpOnly `session_token` cookie, which Postman stores automatically — you do not need to copy a token anywhere.

Set `userEmail` and `userPassword` in your environment first. Passwords must be at least 12 characters to satisfy the Keycloak realm policy.

Rate limited to 10/min, and 3 *failed* attempts per (IP, email) trips a temporary 429 block.

Themed email + password login (direct grant). The GET /login above keeps
the OIDC redirect flow for SSO.

`POST /auth/login`

exec: console.log('Signed in as', me.email, '- role:', me.role);
console.log('The session_token cookie is now in the jar; other requests will use it.');

request.description:
Self-service signup. Students activate immediately; teachers are created
as students with pending_teacher=true, awaiting admin approval.

`POST /auth/signup`

Confirm a signup verification code and mark the account email-verified.
On success the client logs in normally (POST /auth/login).

`POST /auth/verify-email`

Re-send a verification code for a not-yet-verified signup. Always returns
200 (never reveals whether the account exists / is already verified).

`POST /auth/resend-code`

Begin a password reset. Always returns 200 so the response can't be used
to enumerate which emails have accounts.

`POST /auth/forgot-password`

Complete a password reset with the emailed code, then set the new
password in Keycloak. The client logs in afterwards.

`POST /auth/reset-password`

Browser-only. Keycloak redirects here after SSO; not callable directly.

Handle OIDC callback — verify state, exchange with PKCE, gate by domain.

`GET /auth/callback`

Use the refresh_token cookie to mint a new access token.

Origin is checked even though the cookie is HttpOnly — defence-in-depth
against a CSRF flow that drives the browser to /auth/refresh from a
malicious origin in our CORS allowlist.

`POST /auth/refresh`
`GET /auth/me`

RP-initiated logout against Keycloak.

Revokes the refresh token, clears local cookies, and redirects to the
Keycloak `end_session_endpoint` so the SSO session is also killed. Without
this, the user can hit /auth/login and be SSO'd back in without entering
credentials.

`POST /auth/logout`

List the caller's API keys (prefix only — secrets are never stored).

`GET /auth/api-keys`

Returns the plaintext key **once** — only its SHA-256 hash is stored, so a lost key must be revoked and recreated. The test script saves it into the `apiKey` variable for you.

Requires a real cookie session: you cannot mint a new key using an existing API key. `read_only` scope is restricted to GET/HEAD/OPTIONS; use `full_access` if you need to create or delete things.

Generate a scoped API key. The plaintext key is returned ONCE here and
only its SHA-256 hash is stored — copy it now or revoke and re-create.

`POST /auth/api-keys`

exec: // The plaintext key is returned exactly once. Store it now.
console.log('Saved apiKey. Copy it somewhere safe - it is not retrievable again.');

request.description:
Revoke one of the caller's API keys (soft delete, idempotent).

Set `{{keyId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`DELETE /auth/api-keys/{key_id}`

item.name: 2. VMs (pods)
item.description:
A pod is a VM. `Create VM` returns immediately and the VM boots asynchronously, so poll `Get VM` until `state` is `running`.

If the cluster is full the request is queued rather than rejected — check `Queue position` and `Availability`. `Create VM` saves the new id into the `podId` variable, so the rest of this folder targets it without editing.

request.description:
List available VM plans (admin-managed catalogue) with resources + pricing.

`GET /pods/plans`

List available (active) VM templates with their resolved image + metadata.

`GET /pods/templates`

List VMs for the current user.

`GET /pods/`

exec: console.log('Seeded podId from the first VM:', pods[0].id);

request.description:
Creates a VM. Returns immediately — the VM boots asynchronously, so poll `Get VM` until `state` is `running`.

If the cluster has no room the request is admitted to a queue instead of failing; the response carries a queue position. `plan` is one of `small`, `medium`, `large`. `template` is one of `ubuntu`, `python-ml`, `cpp`, `java`. Leave `image` null to use the template's default image.

Create a new VM instance.

This allocates a slice of the host machine's CPU/RAM to the user as an
isolated container with SSH access. Resources are capped by the chosen plan.

`POST /pods/`

exec: console.log('Cluster is full; queued at position', body.queue_position);

request.description:
Free capacity across the cluster. A VM reserves a quarter of its plan's CPU and bursts to the full limit when cores are idle, so the reserved figure is what admission actually checks against.

Best-effort cluster capacity readout for the VM create UI.

Never 500s: if the orchestrator is unreachable the capacity fields come
back null while the queue length (read straight from the DB) stays real.

`GET /pods/availability`

List the caller's own pending queue entries (queued/admitting).

`GET /pods/queue`

Cancel a still-queued VM request owned by the caller.

Only a 'queued' entry can be cancelled: once it is 'admitting' the
orchestrator create is already in flight, so we refuse with 409.

Set `{{queueEntryId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`DELETE /pods/queue/{entry_id}`

Get VM details.

Set `{{podId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`GET /pods/{pod_id}`

Terminate a VM.

Set `{{podId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`DELETE /pods/{pod_id}`

Stream CPU/RAM metrics via SSE.

The orchestrator publishes metrics on subject ``metrics.<pod_name>`` where
pod_name is the orchestrator-side identifier (``vm-<unix_nano>``), not the
API UUID we use in URLs. We resolve session.pod_name here so the
subscription actually matches what's being published.

Set `{{podId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`GET /pods/{pod_id}/metrics`

item.name: 3. Credits
item.description: Credit balances and transfers. Admins allocate to teachers, teachers allocate to their students. VMs bill per hour against the owner's balance while they are in the `running` state.

request.description:
Get current credit balance.

`GET /credits/balance`

Get credit transaction history.

`GET /credits/history`

Teachers (professors) with balances — for the admin grant view.

`GET /credits/teachers`

Students with balances — for the teacher allocation view.

`GET /credits/students`

Admins allocate to teachers; teachers allocate to their own students. Allocating to a user outside your scope returns 403.

Credit delegation, role-aware:

- **admin** grants credits to a user from the system account (used to fund
  teachers). This can't overdraw — the system account is the ledger source.
- **professor** allocates from *their own* balance to a student, and is
  rejected with 402 if they lack the credits.

`POST /credits/allocate`

item.name: 4. Usage & metrics
item.description: Per-VM resource samples and the aggregated series behind the dashboard charts.

request.description:
Get time-series usage data for a pod.

Uses TimescaleDB time_bucket for efficient aggregation.
Falls back to simple GROUP BY if TimescaleDB is not available.

Set `{{podId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`GET /usage/{pod_id}`

Aggregated time-series across all of the current user's pods.

Used by the dashboard to show busyness over time instead of a single
snapshot. Bucket size scales with the requested range so the response
stays small enough to render directly without client-side downsampling.

`GET /usage/summary/me/series`

Get usage summary for the current user.

`GET /usage/summary/me`

item.name: 5. Files
item.description: Browse, upload and download files inside a running VM's workspace.

request.description:
List a directory inside the VM so the UI can render a browser.

Returned entries: {name, is_dir, size, mtime}. Sorted: dirs first then
files, both case-insensitive alpha. The path is quoted before being
inlined into the remote command — never substituted raw — so a filename
with spaces or quotes can't break out of the ls argument.

Set `{{podId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`GET /files/{pod_id}/list`

multipart/form-data. Pick a local file for the `file` form field in Postman's Body tab before sending; the exported collection cannot embed file contents.

Upload a file to the VM via SCP.

Set `{{podId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`POST /files/{pod_id}/upload`

formdata.description: Choose a local file in Postman's Body tab.

request.description:
Download a file from the VM via SCP.

Set `{{podId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`GET /files/{pod_id}/download`

item.name: 6. SSH keys
item.description: Public keys injected into VMs at boot so you can SSH in directly.

request.description:
List user's SSH public keys.

`GET /ssh-keys/`

Add an SSH public key.

`POST /ssh-keys/`

Delete an SSH key.

Set `{{keyId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`DELETE /ssh-keys/{key_id}`

item.name: 7. Settings
item.description: Per-user preferences, currently the VS Code editor settings blob.

request.description:
Return the user's persisted VS Code settings blob ({} if none saved).

`GET /settings/vscode`

Persist the user's VS Code settings blob (per-user, upserted).

Previously this accepted the body and discarded it. It is now stored in the
DB so it survives across sessions (a future enhancement can sync it into the
VM's code-server config on launch).

`PUT /settings/vscode`

item.name: 8. Notifications
item.description: In-app notifications. `Stream` is Server-Sent Events — Postman shows it as a long-running response rather than a normal JSON body.

request.description:
Recent notifications for the current user, newest first.

`GET /notifications/`

Mark every notification for the current user as read.

`POST /notifications/read-all`

Mark a single notification as read.

Set `{{notificationId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`POST /notifications/{notification_id}/read`

Server-Sent Events. This response never completes — Postman will show it streaming until you cancel it. That is expected, not a hang.

Live notification stream (SSE) for the current user.

`GET /notifications/stream`

item.name: 9. Issues
item.description: Student-reported problems and the admin queue that resolves them.

request.description:
Report a problem with an active session.

`POST /issues/`
`GET /issues/me`
`GET /issues/admin`

Set `{{issueId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`POST /issues/admin/{issue_id}/resolve`

item.name: 10. Admin
item.description:
Admin-only. A non-admin session gets 403 on every request in this folder.

Covers user and role management, teacher approvals, the plan and image catalogues, cluster nodes, audit logs and platform stats.

request.description:
List all users (admin only).

`GET /admin/users`

Users who signed up as a teacher and await approval (admin only).

`GET /admin/teacher-requests`

Approve a pending teacher: promote to professor and clear the flag.

Set `{{userId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`POST /admin/teacher-requests/{user_id}/approve`

Reject a pending teacher: clear the flag, the user stays a student.

Set `{{userId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`POST /admin/teacher-requests/{user_id}/reject`

List courses and their resource quotas.

Not yet implemented — no course model in the DB.
Returns an empty list for the POC.

`GET /admin/courses`

List compute nodes and their resource usage.

Calls the orchestrator's ListNodes gRPC to get real K8s node info
including CPU/memory capacity, allocatable resources, and pod counts.

`GET /admin/nodes`

Dashboard stats: total users, active VMs, etc.

`GET /admin/stats`

List currently active VMs across all users with owner email/name.

`GET /admin/active-vms`

Change a user's app role.

Updates Keycloak (canonical source) first, then mirrors to the local
`users.role` column, then force-logs-out the user so their next request
receives a JWT with the new role. Refuses to:
  - demote yourself
  - drop the admin count to zero
  - assign an unknown role
Writes an audit_logs row with old/new role for accountability.

Set `{{userId}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`PATCH /admin/users/{user_id}/role`

View audit logs (admin only).

`GET /admin/audit-logs`

List every plan, including inactive ones (admin view).

`GET /admin/plans`

Create a new VM plan.

`POST /admin/plans`

Update a plan's resources / pricing / active flag (name is immutable).

Set `{{planName}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`PUT /admin/plans/{name}`

Soft-delete (deactivate) a plan. Existing pods on it keep billing.

Set `{{planName}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`DELETE /admin/plans/{name}`

List every image/template, including inactive ones (admin view).

`GET /admin/images`

Create a new VM template → image mapping.

`POST /admin/images`

Update a template's image / metadata / active + default flags.

Set `{{imageTemplate}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`PUT /admin/images/{template}`

Soft-delete (deactivate) a template.

Set `{{imageTemplate}}` in your environment or let an earlier request populate it.

`DELETE /admin/images/{template}`

item.name: 11. Health probes
item.description: Unauthenticated probes. `/healthz` is liveness (shallow by design — restarting the pod cannot fix a down database). `/readyz` is readiness and returns 503 with a per-dependency breakdown when the gateway cannot serve real traffic.

request.description: `GET /healthz`
`GET /readyz`
